extracted.intended_audience: NSF proposal authors (PIs/co-PIs), NSF reviewers (panelists/ad hoc reviewers), and NSF Program Officers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on preparing, reviewing, and processing NSF proposals, including administrative compliance, the two merit review criteria (Intellectual Merit and Broader Impacts), the five review elements, conflicts of interest, review types, and funding/award considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary compliance review (completeness/timeliness/format)
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receipt at NSF, proposals are routed to the PI-designated program office. NSF staff conducts a preliminary review to ensure they are: Complete; Timely; and Conform to proposal preparation requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NSF may not accept a proposal or may return it without review if it does not meet the requirements above. If the proposal is outside the scope of the program, the Program Officer usually tries his/her best to transfer it to the most appropriate program for evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: PAPPG Project Summary Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Project Summary must include an overview and separate statements on Intellectual Merit and Broader Impacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to include these required statements can result in the proposal being returned without review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Description Broader Impacts section
rubrics_metrics.description: The Project Description must contain, as a separate section within the narrative, a section labeled 'Broader Impacts.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Omitting a separate Broader Impacts section is a basis for return without review. The Project Description must also include results from prior NSF support with an end date in the past five years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Management Plan requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A Data Management Plan must be included as a supplementary document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Missing the Data Management Plan per PAPPG is a reason to return the proposal without review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postdoctoral Researcher Mentoring Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals that include postdoctoral researchers must include a description of the mentoring activities that will be provided for such individuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicable, failure to include the mentoring description can lead to the proposal being returned without review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative/formatting requirements (page limits, electronic submission, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals must meet NSF proposal preparation requirements, such as page limitations, formatting instructions, and electronic submission, as specified in the PAPPG or program solicitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Noncompliance with these requirements is a ground for return without review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsiveness to program solicitation / scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals must be responsive to the PAPPG or program announcement/solicitation and appropriate for funding by the National Science Foundation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals that are not responsive or are inappropriate for NSF funding may be returned without review; if outside scope, a Program Officer may attempt to transfer it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness and lead time
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals must meet announced proposal deadline dates (and times where specified) and be submitted with sufficient lead time before the activity is scheduled to begin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insufficient lead time or missed deadlines can result in return without review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duplicate/substantially similar and prior-declined submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: A proposal that is a duplicate of, or substantially similar to, a proposal already under consideration by NSF from the same submitter; duplicates of awarded proposals; or a full proposal submitted after a 'not invited' response to a preliminary proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such submissions are grounds for return without review. Also, proposals previously reviewed and declined that have not been substantially revised may be returned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merit Review Guiding Principles
rubrics_metrics.description: All NSF projects should be of the highest quality and have the potential to advance, if not transform, the frontiers of knowledge. NSF projects, in the aggregate, should contribute more broadly to achieving societal goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meaningful assessment and evaluation of NSF-funded projects should be based on appropriate metrics, keeping in mind the likely correlation between the effect of broader impacts and the resources provided to implement projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellectual Merit (primary review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Intellectual Merit criterion encompasses the potential to advance knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating proposals, reviewers should consider what proposers want to do, why, how they plan to do it, how they will know if they succeed, and what benefits would accrue if the project is successful — for the technical aspects of the proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broader Impacts (primary review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Broader Impacts criterion encompasses the potential to benefit society and contribute to the achievement of specific, desired societal outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers evaluate Broader Impacts alongside Intellectual Merit; proposers should explicitly address broader societal contributions in the Project Summary and a separate Broader Impacts section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review Element: Potential to advance knowledge / benefit society
rubrics_metrics.description: What is the potential for the proposed activity to advance knowledge and understanding within its own field or across different fields (Intellectual Merit) and to benefit society or advance desired societal outcomes (Broader Impacts)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This element is to be considered for both criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review Element: Creativity / transformative potential
rubrics_metrics.description: To what extent do the proposed activities suggest and explore creative, original, or potentially transformative concepts?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should explicitly evaluate novelty/originality and transformative potential under both criteria where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review Element: Quality of the project plan and assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the plan for carrying out the proposed activities well-reasoned, well-organized, and based on a sound rationale? Does the plan incorporate a mechanism to assess success?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A clear mechanism to assess success is expected; weak or poorly organized plans weaken reviews under both criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review Element: Qualifications of personnel and institution
rubrics_metrics.description: How well qualified is the individual, team, or institution to conduct the proposed activities?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer assessments should consider PI/co-PI track records, team composition, and institutional capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review Element: Adequacy of resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Are there adequate resources available to the PI (either at the home institution or through collaborations) to carry out the proposed activities?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include evaluation of institutional support, facilities, collaborations, and budget realism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer role: scope of review and comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Review all proposal material and consider the two NSF merit review criteria and any program-specific criteria, the adequacy of the proposed project plan including the budget, resources, and timeline, the priorities of the scientific field and of the NSF program, and the potential risks and benefits of the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should make independent written comments on the quality of the proposal content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of review formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals may be reviewed as Ad hoc (external experts), Panel (face-to-face sessions by reviewers), Combination (panel plus supplemental ad hoc reviews), or Internal (review by NSF Program Officers only).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some proposals may undergo only one type of review or multiple reviews (e.g., crosscutting themes may see multiple panels). Examples of internally reviewed proposals are listed (e.g., RAPID, EAGER, RAISE, CLB supplements, conferences under $50,000).

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of reviewers (expertise and sources)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers recruited include those with specific content expertise and those with general science or education expertise. Sources include Program Officer knowledge, references listed in the proposal, professional society programs, computer searches of relevant journal articles, former reviewers, and reviewer recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understanding reviewer sourcing helps proposers tailor submissions and suggest appropriate reviewers when requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Managing conflicts of interest — purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary purpose is to remove or limit the influence of ties to an applicant institution or investigator that could affect reviewer advice. Secondary purpose is to preserve trust in the integrity, effectiveness, and evenhandedness of NSF’s merit review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers must disclose conflicts and recuse as required to protect process integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affiliations with applicant institutions (examples of conflicts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples: Current employment at the institution; other associations such as being a consultant; being considered for employment or any formal or informal reemployment arrangement; any office, governing board membership, or relevant committee membership at the institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such affiliations are considered conflicts and typically preclude participation in review of the proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal relationships with investigator or project director (examples of conflicts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples: Known family or marriage relationship; business partner; past or present thesis advisor or thesis student; collaboration on a project, book, article, or paper within the last 48 months; co-edited a journal, compendium, or conference proceedings within the last 24 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recent collaborations and close personal relationships are treated as conflicts of interest and generally require recusal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Possible considerations for funding a competitive proposal
rubrics_metrics.description: Considerations beyond the review criteria that may influence funding: Addresses all review criteria; Likely high impact; Broadening participation; Educational impact; Impact on institution/state; Special programmatic considerations (e.g., CAREER/RUI/EPSCoR); Other support for PI; 'Launching' versus 'Maintaining'; Portfolio balance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program Officers make funding recommendations guided by program goals and portfolio considerations; Division Directors concur or reject recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feedback provided to proposers from merit review
rubrics_metrics.description: Feedback includes reviewer ratings (such as: E, V, G, F, P), analysis of how well the proposal addresses both review criteria (Intellectual Merit and Broader Impacts), proposal strengths and weaknesses, and reasons for a declination (if applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If questions arise, proposers should contact the cognizant Program Officer for clarification. Feedback may include verbatim copies of reviews (excluding reviewer identities), panel summaries, and PO-to-PI comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation produced by the review process
rubrics_metrics.description: Documentation from merit review may include verbatim copies of individual reviews excluding reviewer identities, Panel Summary or Summaries (if used), a Process Statement (usually), and PO-to-PI comments (formal or informal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These documents explain decisions and provide transparency; proposers should review them carefully to inform resubmissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revisions and resubmissions considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: When deciding whether to resubmit, consider whether reviewers and the Program Officer identify significant strengths in your proposal; whether you can address the weaknesses identified; and other ways you or colleagues can strengthen a resubmission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact the cognizant Program Officer with questions about resubmission strategy.
